correctness_confidence.basis: Checked by hand: polar form (2) of (1); L_fP identity in Lemma 2 and sign of Im h = p'/(2Np) (d/dphi log|1-alpha e^{i phi}|^2 = Im K); Lemma 3 constant term equals 1 (checked symbolically for general c); identities (12)-(13) at test points c=1, z=1 and the pole at z=0; min over c of (a+c)sqrt(1+c^2)/c at c=a^(1/3) giving (1+a^(2/3))^(3/2); Prop 4 error bound 4 pi sigma/(N tau^2) and N<=256 pi b^2/delta^3. No gap found in the main chain. Not checked: boundary regularity of h_c at the two exceptional points (asserted by order counting only); the Corollary 6 k>=2 sketch was checked only at the level of rescaling and the Lyapunov function H; no code was run.

rigor.basis: Necessity (Section 3) and sufficiency (Sections 4-5, Proposition 4) are explicit and quantified; equality excluded; local analytic case (Section 6) reduced to the homogeneous case with a correct integrating-factor argument. Weaker parts: Proposition 5 is a compactness argument without a rate; Lemma 3 boundary claims at eta-bar and eta^3 are sketched; Corollary 6 for general k is argued by reduction to k=1 with the same steps, not written out in full.

novelty.basis: The exact threshold |b|^(2/3) < 1 + a^(2/3) is new relative to the cited obstruction 2(a+1) in [1], which the paper itself describes as only sufficient. Novelty of the degree-divergence statement (Prop 5) and of the SOS consequence (Cor 7) is weaker and depends on [2]. I could not confirm from the abstract page that [1] states the family, the 2(a+1) obstruction, or GAS for the parametrized family; the arXiv abstract of 2607.16171 confirms only the cubic GAS example with no polynomial and no local analytic Lyapunov function. The statement of [2] Theorem 4.3 (unbounded minimum degree in fixed dimension and degree) is confirmed by the abstract only, not its theorem numbering. Not verified: Ahmadi and El Khadir Prop 6.1 and Lemma 6.2.

significance.basis: A sharp, checkable threshold for a specific cubic family plus a clean characterization of four certificate classes is a substantive contribution to converse Lyapunov theory. Significance is limited to one family and to the homogeneous setting; the general multiharmonic classification and the minimum degree rate are explicitly left open by the paper.

reproducibility.basis: The main results are analytic and the constructions are explicit (Lemma 3 formulas, Proposition 4 degree bound), so the proofs can be reproduced by hand. The numerical diagnostics (2048-factor product at a=1.2, b=2 sqrt 2, sampled margin about 0.1545; 18 Toeplitz relaxations) have no code, seeds, solver logs or data attached, and the paper says they are not certificates. Rigorous quantile enclosures are not supplied.

summary: The manuscript studies r' = r^3(-a + b cos 2theta), theta' = r^2 (the Liu-Fitzsimmons cubic family, with a > 0 and b real) and claims that positive homogeneous polynomial weak certificates, strict polynomial certificates (finite products of positive quadratic forms), and local real-analytic weak certificates exist exactly when |b| < (1+a^(2/3))^(3/2). The necessity direction uses a positive harmonic function u with mean 1 and a test function built from a square root of a Mobius-type expression; minimizing over the test parameter c gives the bound and equality is excluded. Sufficiency uses Herglotz representation, Poisson smoothing, a boundary limiting pair at (c^3, s^3), quantile discretization with an explicit degree bound N <= 256 pi b^2 / delta^3, and Fejer-Riesz factorization. I checked the main algebraic identities and the optimization in the necessity argument and found them consistent. Proposition 5 (degree divergence at the threshold) and the SOS corollary are correct in outline but nonconstructive or dependent on cited results. Numerical diagnostics are explicitly non-certifying and are not reproducible from the manuscript. Novelty against [1] and [2] depends on citations that I could only partly confirm.
strengths: Sharp two-sided characterization of a specific family, with equality excluded even for weak certificates.
Necessity argument is short and explicit: pointwise bound uF+wG >= eps F, then sigma to 1, then minimization over c with unique critical point c = a^(1/3).
Explicit sufficient degree bound with an elementary error estimate (derivative of the Cayley kernel, equal-mass quantiles).
Local analytic case reduced to the homogeneous case by a correct leading-term and integrating-factor argument.
The paper states clearly what is not claimed: no minimum-degree rate, no certified numerics, no general multiharmonic classification.
weaknesses: Lemma 3 boundary behaviour at the two exceptional points (zero of M_c at eta^3 and pole at eta-bar) is argued by order counting only; a short explicit expansion would make the limiting pair fully verifiable.

Corollary 6 for k >= 2 is obtained by reduction to k = 1 and is not written out; the claim that all fields in (18) are globally asymptotically stable is correct in my reading but needs the argument stated.
Proposition 5 gives only non-constructive divergence; the abstract's phrase about the minimum degree should not be read as a rate.
Numerical diagnostics (2048-factor product, Toeplitz relaxations) have no code, seeds or data and cannot support any claim; they should be removed or clearly labelled as anecdotal.
Novelty relative to [1] depends on a comparison I could not verify from the cited abstract; the paper should quote the exact statement of [1] for the family and the 2(a+1) obstruction.
Theorem numbering for [2] (Theorem 4.3, Section 5, Theorem 5.3) and for [3] (Proposition 6.1, Lemma 6.2) is cited to an author-hosted or non-archival version; the exact statements were not checked.
strong_novelty_candidates: The exact threshold |b|^(2/3) < 1 + a^(2/3) for the family, identifying the same boundary for weak homogeneous, strict product-of-quadratics, and local analytic certificates.
The explicit boundary limiting pair (Lemma 3) with a harmonic pair u_c, w_c having disjoint zero arcs, which is what forces the non-strict endpoint to fail.
